**Rule of engagement.** Isaiah 28:10 sets how this debate is read: "For precept [must be] upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, [and] there a little: [must be: or, hath been]". My case is a chain of interlocking rows, and a challenge must break the chain, not one link. I cite Isaiah 28:10 as the method of reading, never as a witness for a conclusion.

**The answer to the topic.** Yes. Christ had a biological father, and the rows name him: Joseph, of the house of David, the husband of Mary. I lay the account first, so that no reader brings in a reading the rows do not carry.
